candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of Class A versus Class B pathogen requirements depends on how the land-application site type is classified, which changes which monitoring obligations are in scope for Purpose B and how missing or conditional no-result evidence is categorized for Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is applied to a lawn or home garden shall be treated by the Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a use qualifies as lawn or home garden application determines whether only Class A pathogen monitoring applies, affecting Purpose B applicability determinations and Purpose C treatment of periods where conditional monitoring may not be required.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag shall be treated by Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is sold or given away in a bag triggers Class A-only requirements, changing which monitoring is required under Purpose B and how missing-evidence cases are classified under Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: All 6 options require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 Most Probable Number (MPN) per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three MPN per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive either-or structure affects which numeric thresholds govern compliance under Purpose A and whether monitoring for one parameter, both parameters, or either suffices under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when sampling must occur (use/disposal versus bag preparation) change which monitoring periods are obligated under Purpose B and whether absent results reflect conditional non-requirement or missing evidence under Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a facility relies on Alternatives 5 or 6 affects which Class A demonstration pathway—and associated monitoring—is actually authorized, changing Purpose B rows and unresolved cases.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - The temperature of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be maintained at a specific value for a period of time. See 503.32(a)(3)(ii) for specific information.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The operative temperature and duration are incorporated only by cross-reference; whether in-segment text alone establishes the numeric/process limits and monitoring obligations, or leaves them unresolved pending external text, changes Purpose A and B outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the pH threshold, duration, and measurement definition (including the following temperature-conversion language) determines applicable numeric/process limits for Purpose A and whether associated monitoring or recordkeeping is required under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conjunctive timing between pH and temperature conditions affects whether multiple numeric/process criteria must all be satisfied and therefore changes enforceable limit evaluation and monitoring applicability.

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The percent-solids threshold is an additional numeric criterion whose timing and measurement basis affect Purpose A comparisons and whether corresponding monitoring is required under Purpose B.

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether analysis must occur prior to treatment establishes a monitoring obligation independent of the numeric limit stated elsewhere in Alternative 3.

candidates.exact_span: The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The numeric limit and the permissive either-before-or-after timing jointly affect which measurements are compared under Purpose A, when monitoring is required under Purpose B, and how absent results are classified when sampling timing is ambiguous under Purpose C.
